summary: Martina Palladino is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned a B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Bologna and an MPhil/PhD at SOAS University of London. She has held posts at Bologna and Ghent University (2023).
Martine Kropman is an Indologist who conducted PhD research at the University of Groningen and at Leiden University (attested 2026) under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop.

Martino Dibeltulo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr., having also studied under mentor Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was an art historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1946–1954), and held a long-standing academic post at the University of Michigan (~1949–1993).
Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Philip Boas Yampolsky.

Mary Belle Harris (1874–1957) was an Indology scholar. She studied at Keystone Academy, Bucknell University, the University of Chicago (Ph.D. in Sanskrit, ~1897–1900), and Johns Hopkins, and taught at the American School of Classical Studies in Rome (1912–1914).

Mary Boyce (1920–2006) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. She studied at Cambridge and SOAS under scholars including Walter Bruno Henning. Her career was based largely at SOAS, where she served as Professor of Iranian Studies (1963–1982).

Mary Cecilia Foley (1859–1925) was active in Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a B.Sc. from University College London (-1891) and served as Chief Lady Invigilator at the University of London from 1901 to 1925.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a scholar of Sinology and history who studied at Vassar and Radcliffe College. She served as curator of Stanford's China collection (1947) before joining Yale University, where she became a full professor in 1964.

Mary Evelyn Tucker (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. Educated at institutions including Columbia (Ph.D.), UCLA, and Duke, she held faculty posts at Bucknell University (~1989–2006) and Yale University (~2006).

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist who studied at Earlham College, the University of Chicago, and Yale University, training under Edward Sapir (~1930–1935). She held a long-term academic post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1977).

Mary Jaksch (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. Educated at Michigan, Columbia (PhD), NYU, and Harvard, she worked for the U.S. Department of State, the National Museum of African Art, and the National Museum of Asian Art.
Marybeth White specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She completed an undergraduate degree at York University and pursued doctoral studies at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).
Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied under Stanisław Schayer (~1932–1937) and held a post at the University of Warsaw (~1937–1939).

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied under mentors Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Marzenna Jakubczak is a philosopher and Indologist. She earned her PhD from Jagiellonian University and her habilitation from Maria Curie-Skłodowska University, later holding posts at the Pedagogical University of Krakow (attested 2012) and Jagiellonian University (Associate Professor, 2024).

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He completed undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at Kyoto University, holding posts there from 1968 to 1993 before serving as professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori (born 1924) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta. He held a primary post in Kyoto University's Faculty of Letters (1961–1988) and numerous international visiting professorships.

Masaaki Nitta (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).
